evidence:
Direct openpyxl inspection of the frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx found Quality Checks!A42:E42: check 41, binary_and_likert_fit_the_ask, 'Pass/fail behaviors are binary; craft and degree-of-quality are likert with described anchors.' Internal Quality Checks row 42 contains the historical binary/weighted-only annotation. The frozen rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md, Known false positives, and references/quality-checks.md:168-170 explicitly resolve that annotation in favor of the shipped binary/Likert format. The staged contract's judge.toml section permits scored Likert with points=5 and requires binary gates.

All task/rules citations below are relative to .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/. Parsed every one of the five task/tests/*/*/judge.toml files with Python 3.12 tomllib: Render has 1 binary, Constraints 1 binary, Functional 64 binary, Polish 7 binary, and Visual 6 Likert criteria (79 total; 73 binary). Every Likert has points=5 and exactly one nonempty anchor for each integer 1 through 5; no missing or duplicate level was found. Read all criterion descriptions and the relevant injected/public instructions. Recomputed every frozen task and rules manifest file hash; all 50 task and 34 rules files match the manifest, as does the current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md.

The binary criteria ask whether concrete behavior occurs. Render's authored marker must appear in preview and console (task/tests/gates/render/judge.toml:20-27), and Constraints requires an exact saved record read in an independent clean context (task/tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:20-29). Functional describes execution, source dispatch, console evidence, deadlines, rollback, storage, revision conflicts and explicit editor features. For example cw_editor_monospace/cw_editor_line_numbers/cw_editor_syntax_colouring are binary feature checks (task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:310-329), directly requested by task/environment/instructions/ui.md:5. The protocol accepts any syntax palette and editor implementation (task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:385-391). Actual theme changes and work retention are binary (functional/judge.toml:401-413); the protocol explicitly assigns contrast, palette and aesthetic readability to Visual (functional/prompt.md:442). The shared-scenario contract at functional/prompt.md:98-100 preserves independently observed binary results, consistent with qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md, Independent credit.

Reviewed every Polish row for a binary craft threshold. These are minimum usability predicates: reach/use each pane on mobile; identify controls; reach them by keyboard; observe focus; complete the keyboard library route; obtain visible acknowledgement of an ordinary action; and identify editable-code/output/saved-work surfaces. task/tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:23 accepts stacking, tabs, drawers and intentional scrolling. Lines 50 and 59 accept native outlines and standard editor escape. Lines 68 and 77 concern acknowledgement and locating/identifying surfaces, rather than demanding a particular degree of aesthetic refinement. Their separation from visual degree is explicit in task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:13-22. These descriptions do not convert broad visual craft into an all-or-nothing score.

Visual contains the six actual craft dimensions: typography, color/contrast, spacing/layout, hierarchy/scannability, overall consistency, and responsive composition. Each is Likert (task/tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:17-105). For example typography has full readable/consistent treatment at 5, a few distracting issues at 4, several issues slowing scanning at 3, substantial reading difficulty at 2, and largely unreadable/nonrendering at 1 (lines 24-29). The same explicit 5-to-1 gradation exists at lines 39-44, 54-59, 69-74, 84-89 and 99-104. The prompt requires integer anchors 1 through 5 and explains the (raw-1)/4 normalization (visual/prompt.md:39-43); its failed prerequisite uses raw 1, not raw 0 (lines 31-32).

Adversarial source-level checks: a conforming simple app with native controls/outlines, standard editor escape, stacked mobile panes, and a restrained palette is expressly eligible for full credit (Polish lines 23, 50, 59; Visual lines 40, 55, 85 and 99-100). Cosmetic imperfections need not collapse functional or usability credit; moderate visual issues map to anchors 3/4. Conversely, an attractive interface with a keyboard-inaccessible library cannot gain the binary navigation/reachability points merely through appearance (Polish lines 41, 59), and a fully functional app with substantial unreadable text is assigned low typography anchors (Visual lines 27-29), rather than full craft credit for rendering. Neither attempted witness exposes a type/anchor false pass or false fail. These are rubric interpretation checks, not measured model executions.

This Pass concerns row 41's authored scoring types and anchors only. The raw-evidence index expressly lacks a full configured judge, Oracle or target-model run; I did not infer runtime normalization compatibility, judge behavior, score discrimination or timing from static parsing or scripted golden evidence.
